sense.text:
The old books say it plainly. One from 1860 says the social position of the negro in Egypt 3,500 years ago was the same as it is now in the United States: a stranger, an alien in a foreign land, slaves at Thebes and Memphis, Babylon and Nineveh, Rome, Athens, Carthage, Constantinople, Havana and Richmond, slaves at all times and in all places. Others place a most populous nation of the Jewish stock in Africa, a land of the Hebrews between Abyssinia and the Congo, Jews on both sides of the river Niger and on the coast of Guinea who fled there from the desolation of Jerusalem by Vespasian, Jews in Timbuktu who are Muslims now, and Arabic-speaking Jews in West Africa. Like the slaves speaking Arabic in Roots: they were Muslims, but not Arabs; they were Jews forced to take on Islam. So when we say the Israelites are in Africa, we have proof, biblical and from their own old books.

Jeremiah asks the same thing: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” Why is Israel always a servant, always in slavery? Because we keep breaking God’s commandments. We don’t learn our lesson.
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book.” That book is called the Bible today.

“I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, saith the Lord: and I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” To bring again the captivity is to bring Israel back from captivity, not into captivity. He brings us back to the land he gave our fathers, and we shall possess it.

“We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.” We are coming up on that moment now, and there is a voice of fear and trembling.

Our people cheer Martin Luther King and Malcolm X in the movies, and now there is a campaign to besmirch them: Martin an adulterer, Malcolm gay. It starts with white people, and now black people are getting paid to spin that narrative. You may not have agreed with Martin’s method, but how many of us would walk down the street knowing we would get the hell beat out of us, thrown in jail and have dogs set on us? Because of men like that, Jim Crow ended. We were seen as three-fifths, carrying signs that said I am a man; since 1965 we have had about 60 years of a liberty we did not have before. And how have we used it? We shoot each other, besmirch one another and hate each other, and the white man says, they were better off under us. Two young boys were shot in the face in our Georgia camp, and it wasn’t the white man; it was a black brother.

Our people side with the resistance in The Hunger Games, Star Wars, The Matrix and V for Vendetta, but when it is happening to them in real life they are afraid to resist. They won’t speak up for our people in Sudan or talk about Cuba, they would never have joined Malcolm or Martin, and a lot of them won’t join us, out of fear. They call us Black Hebrew Israelites, a term coined by the oppressor, while we go to our people in Nigeria, Italy, South Africa, Kenya, Ghana, Sierra Leone, Haiti and the Caribbean, telling them to come out of her. That is the voice of fear, and not of peace.

“Wherefore do I see every man with his hands on his loins, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned into paleness?” Jeremiah sees a vision of the Israelite men holding their loins like a woman in labour, their faces gone pale with fear.

“Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” Jacob’s trouble is the great tribulation coming on Israel, a day like no other. Pause right there and go to what Christ said about it in Matthew 10. We keep coming back to this verse: what makes this tribulation different from all the others, and how Israel “shall be saved out of it.”

precepts.why:
Some brothers read Joel and get confused: “For, behold, in those days, and in that time, when I shall bring again the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem”. Read by itself, it sounds like the Lord is bringing us back into slavery. That is not what it means.

Jeremiah 30:3 uses the same words and explains them: “I will bring again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah”, and then, “I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.” Bringing again the captivity is bringing Israel back from captivity to the land, not into captivity.

Our people talk smack like podcasters. Jeremiah said, “Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them!” He wanted to leave black people. Why? “For they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.”

“And they bend their tongues like their bow for lies”: black people love to use their black lips for lies. “But they are not valiant for the truth upon the earth.” There are a lot of black men like the two in the clip, calling themselves revolutionaries and black liberation while they include homosexuality and transgenderism, who are not valiant for the truth. The two young boys shot in Georgia: it was instigated by a gaggle of other black men, and when the cops came they all scattered like cockroaches and played innocent.

They are valiant in the movie theater. They cheer Nat Turner in The Birth of a Nation, they cheer Malcolm X, they cheer Martin Luther King, but they don’t have that spirit on them, and they don’t have the balls to do what he did. “For they proceed from evil to evil, and they know not me, saith the Lord.” That is why there is a voice of trembling and fear among our people, and not of peace.

sense.text:
“And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death.” You don’t believe that could happen while your children are small and cute and adorable, but some of our kids grow up to become demons, haters of God. Samuel’s sons were wicked as hell, so the people said they could not judge Israel; Eli the high priest’s sons were sleeping with all the women. You raise your children the best you can, but what spirit they draw to, only time will tell. You can see a glimpse while they are young: which one is a constant liar, which one is always doing something they have no business doing. As parents you see it, but some of you turn a blind eye to it. You know which child is going to grow up and be no good; you know which little girl is going to be a hoe. You can see it.

A sister held on to a daughter who didn’t want to keep the commandments; she wanted to do TikTok videos, twerk and wear spandex. The girl told her teacher her mother beat her, which was a lie, the police arrested the mother, and now she has a record for violence. When these children show you they hate God, believe them. God don’t want nobody he has to force to serve him.

And “the father the child”: devout black Christian parents have called child protective services on their own children, who keep the commandments, to take the grandkids away, saying they won’t let the children celebrate Christmas. You love your parents, but some of your parents are no damn good. We haven’t seen the death part yet, but that is going to come. This is what Christ says will happen.

“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake”. Every man, woman, boy and girl must understand this about being an Israelite in this truth. As Malcolm said, they are not asking whether one group is Muslim and one Christian. They hate the way we look, because they know we are the chosen people of God. That has been the problem from the beginning: white people look at black people and see God in us. We don’t see God in each other, but they see God in us, and the devil in them hates it.

How will that happen? Propaganda. They control the media; Israel now jails people for showing the bombings in Tel Aviv. They could put a purple shirt on some negro doing terrorist things and call us domestic terrorists, and people will say, I knew they were no damn good. Brothers arrested at their jobs show up in the arrest picture in a purple shirt they were not wearing, and clips from eight or nine years ago are kept up to put us in a bad light. That is how Esau does in his media.

“But he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” We have to endure in this truth to the very end.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another”. Not every city will be chaotic at once; some cities will be going off on the Israelites and some will not. “Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come”: we will not have reached all twelve tribes, all the Israelites, till the Son of man comes.

“The disciple is not above his master, nor the servant above his lord.” The word disciple means student. We are the students; we are not above Christ our master. “If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?” They called Christ Beelzebub, the lord of the flies, a devil, a demon. He is warning us: they are going to do the same thing to you that follow me.

“Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known.” That is why the Epstein files and all these things are popping up. Whatever they have hidden is going to come up.

“What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light”: what he told us in secret, say it in front of everybody. “And what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.” When you have the proper understanding, you go on the housetop and preach it to everybody.

“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”. Christ didn’t change subjects. The things we are going to be teaching will get us killed. People are not going to like you. Speak against America, read Revelation 18 about the fall and destruction of America, and you can be looked at as a domestic terrorist. The whole thing is turning against us, but that is the prophecy. Remember the fear and trembling of Jeremiah 30: that is Jacob’s trouble, and this is what Christ is going into here.

They can’t kill the real you. That body is just a shell that corrodes in time. Death, the Bible calls sleep, and you wake up before the Lord.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the lake of fire, and it is not now. When you die now, everybody is at rest, even the wicked. When the Lord returns he takes the key of hell and death and opens it all up, and that is when the lake of fire comes.

“Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.” A bird doesn’t drop out of the sky without the Father. Nobody dies until the Father says it is time. “But the very hairs of your head are all numbered”: that is how important we are. “Ye are of more value than many sparrows.”

“Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.” Under what conditions? Read in context, he is not talking about you at work saying, yeah, I believe in God. He is talking about tribulation, times of persecution, Jacob’s trouble.

“But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Under tribulation, persecution, Jacob’s trouble, some will say: I never believed that Israelite stuff, I don’t believe in those commandments, my husband forced me, my wife forced me. Him will Christ deny before his Father.

precepts.why:
“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people.” Slavery, miseducation and religion are part of that crafty counsel. Their religions make you think this life is all there is, like the Sam Cooke song: I don’t know what’s up there beyond the sky. If you die you’re going into hell and burn. It puts a fear spirit on you, and everybody is afraid to die.

But when you read the Bible, our foremothers and forefathers didn’t have that spirit. They knew something we didn’t know. The woman with the seven sons said, kill me now, cut my arms off, cut my tongue. Esau’s crafty counsel has taught us lie after lie about reality: that this is it, after this you’re done. The Bible calls death sleep, and you wake up before the Lord. Paul said to be absent in the body is to be present with the Lord. Do we believe that, or what the white man says on his television screens?

That is why Christ says fear not them which kill the body: they can’t touch the real you.

Paul gives his testimony of what he did in the midst of sin: “many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.” Paul was not the only persecutor. Like the inquisitors of Spain and Portugal under Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand, whose job was to hunt down Israelites keeping the commandments, into Africa, Mexico, South America and North America, what Paul did, they were all doing.

“And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”. Compel means he forced them to blaspheme. That is what Christ meant: if you deny me before men, I will deny you, under torture, persecution, tribulation and hard times. That is the trial all of us alive at this time must go through.

Everybody in here says they believe the Lord and love God, but some are liars, not valiant for the truth: professional students, hirelings, like the hireling Christ spoke of who sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep. In the movie Unthinkable a terrorist would not confess where the bombs were until they brought in his wife and kids and did evil things to them. You think that could never happen to you. The devil is a liar. What Paul said he was doing is what Christ says is going to happen.

“And being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” That is why Christ said, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another.

sense.text: “Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name’s sake.” We were just in Matthew 10; now in Matthew 24 Christ repeats the same thing, so we understand what is going to happen. “And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another.”

“And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many.” “And because iniquity shall abound”: iniquity abounds because of the false prophets, the false Christians and these foolish Abrahamic religions teaching lie after lie and glorifying sin. “The love of many shall wax cold”: we are going to start to hate one another.
“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” We have to endure the hardships, the tribulation and the persecution Christ said would come.

“And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.” In Matthew 10 Christ said we would not have gone over the cities of Israel till the Son of man comes, so this is not every Israelite being reached before the end. The ones who preach it in all the world are the 144,000. Once the 144 are sealed, then the end shall come, and they go out to the Israelites who have not heard.

“Immediately after the tribulation of those days”. Churches argue about a seven-year dispensation, pre-trib and post-trib, and say the church is not going through tribulation. You stupid as hell. You don’t know the Bible. Christ says after the tribulation of those days. Those of us that are alive must and will go through tribulation.

“Shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven”: those stars are missiles and rockets. “And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: that is war, war with Idumea, all the Idumean nations at war. The powers of the heavens, with an s, plural, is not talking about the sky.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven”. Look at the order: verse 29, tribulation, then war on earth; verse 30, Christ comes. World War II, from when America entered, was a five-year war; this war might be five years or seven, it doesn’t say. So don’t think Christ might come tomorrow. Where is the tribulation? You can’t pay your light bill; that is not tribulation. Christ is not returning this year or next year. Bad things have to happen first; we have to be proven. Our people are too comfortable, still smoking weed, going to the club and defiling the Sabbath, the women still dressed like hoes with no clothes, and things have to get bad on this earth for them to say the only way is God’s way. In their affliction they will seek him.

“And then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn”: it is going to be a happy day, but we are going to be crying and fearful too.

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.” This is not everybody already gathered by the preaching: in Isaiah 66 there are Israelites who have not heard and have not seen, and we have to go get them. The elect are Israel.

precepts.why:
The angel told Ezra, “But iniquity shall be increased above that which now thou seest, or that thou hast heard long ago.” Iniquity would go way beyond anything he had known or seen. Now men cut their privates off and have a vagina cut in; women get penises sewn on. That was unheard of. Magic Johnson’s son says he is only attracted to straight men; if a man is attracted to you, he is not straight. You can’t make this stuff up.

That is the iniquity that abounds in the last days, and why the love of many waxes cold.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” Christ said we are not going to reach all the Israelites. Some picked that up and some didn’t.

So “this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world” cannot mean every Israelite hears it before the end. Revelation 7 and Isaiah 66 open it: the 144,000 are sealed, then the end comes, and they are sent to those who have not heard.

Remember, the 144 have to get sealed, and then the end comes. “And I will set a sign among them, and I will send those that escape of them unto the nations”: write it down, those that escape are the 144. He sends them to Tarshish, which is Spain; Pul, Libya; Lud, Lydia; Tubal, Turkey; and Javan, the Grecian islands; “to the isles afar off, that have not heard my fame, neither have seen my glory”. There will be Israelites who have not heard the fame of the Lord nor seen his glory, “and they shall declare my glory among the Gentiles.”

This is not talking about now. “And they shall bring all your brethren for an offering unto the Lord out of all nations upon horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and upon mules, and upon swift beasts, to my holy mountain Jerusalem”. Jerusalem is already established and holy here, and Jerusalem is not holy today; it has all kinds of bombs and missiles going off. The 144 take our brethren to the holy Jerusalem, and the Lord says, “And I will also take of them for priests and for Levites”: he makes them priests.

So with a deeper understanding of Matthew 24:14: the gospel preached in all the world for a witness is the 144. Once they are sealed, the end shall come.

“And the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: what powers? “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.” Those are missiles and rockets.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”: so what heaven does Christ bathe his sword in? “Behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”. Idumea is the so-called white man, the leading race on the planet. The powers of the heavens that are shaken are the Idumean nations at war.

“And there shall be signs in the sun”, like the solar eclipse, “and in the moon”, the blood moon, the lunar eclipse, “and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity”. We are seeing that now, and perplexity means confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring” is the nations roaring. “Men’s hearts failing them for fear”, “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: war. Right now we are in verse 25 going into the top of 26.

“And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” Redemption is soon to come, but we know the order of what is going to happen. This is our time to clean ourselves up and get right with the Lord, because time is drawing close.

That same day Iran said it was targeting the Dimona nuclear facility in Israel. Dimona is where the blacks from America went to live, eight miles from a nuclear power plant, with the Ethiopians a few miles down. Many of them told us they don’t believe in Christ, only a prophet. All we can do is pray for our brothers and sisters over there.
“For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”. The elect the angels gather from the four winds is Israel. Not the Baptist church. Not all races on the planet.

sense.text: “I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth”. The winds are the fighting, the wars, the armies. “That the wind should not blow on the earth”: the armies; “nor on the sea”: the marines and the navies; “nor on any tree”: what is above the trees is the air force.

“And I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God”. The four angels were given power to hurt the earth and the sea, to destroy, but the word is “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The end begins when the 144,000 are sealed. That is what Matthew 24:14 means: when they are sealed, then shall the end come.

precepts.why: What the wind is: “And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea”. Out of the four winds come the armies, coming against the Son of God, against the master. So the four winds held back in Revelation 7 are the wars, the armies of the nations.

The seal of the living God is not the hexagram. Some of us thought it was years ago. “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The seal is the law. The servants of God sealed in their foreheads are sealed with his law.

sense.text:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel”. At that time the other gospel was animal sacrifice. Wicked men, scribes and Pharisees, entered the congregations and tried to manipulate them back to the old covenant of animal sacrifice. That is what the book of Galatians is all about.

Today nobody is doing animal sacrifice; the major religions are Christianity and Islam. We come out of that to the truth that we are the Israelites, and then people come around saying, no, go back to Christianity, that’s the truth, or Islam, that’s the truth, and men and women go right back to their filth.

“Which is not another”: those four words mean they used the same scriptures to manipulate and trick the people. Christianity finds all the love scriptures to get you back. Islam takes John 14, the comforter, and says that is Elijah Muhammad, that is Muhammad. Because you don’t study, they use the scriptures to deceive you. “But there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” Christianity perverts the gospel. Islam perverts the gospel.

A Christian clip shows how: Revelation 7:9 is made a glimpse of heaven where God’s kingdom is beautifully diverse, every background and culture, so let’s celebrate our differences and come together. Where was that in 1964? When they were putting us on slave ships using the Bible, why didn’t they say, you can come along? Now that we are bringing this out, all of a sudden let’s all come together, and our people fall for it. We have had 60 years of this little liberty and squandered it, rather than unifying ourselves in the word of God.

“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands”. The Christians say, see, we are all included. But the Bible says precept must be upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little. The number of Israel cannot be numbered; Israelites were dwelling out of every nation under heaven; the Lord recovers the remnant of his people from the four corners of the earth; and Ezra saw this same great people that he could not number upon mount Sion. The great multitude is Israel, out of all the nations they were scattered into. It is Zion.

The 144,000 of verse 4 are the men, Israelite men of the twelve tribes, the leaders. The great multitude are more men, women and children.

They cry “Salvation to our God which sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb.” “And all the angels stood round about the throne”, and fell before the throne on their faces and worshipped God, saying “Blessing, and glory, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, and honour, and power, and might, be unto our God for ever and ever.”

The elder asks, “What are these which are arrayed in white robes? and whence came they?” Who is this great multitude? “These are they which came out of great tribulation”. The churches say we don’t have to go through tribulation; these are they that came out of great tribulation, “and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.” The Bible doesn’t contradict itself. Christianity contradicts the Bible.

precepts.why:
“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”. That’s us. The multitude “which no man could number” is Israel, whose number cannot be numbered.

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Israelites out of every nation under heaven. So “of all nations” in Revelation 7:9 is Israel coming out of all the nations, not all the races.

If you have time on the street, there are many ways to handle this verse. “The Lord shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people”: the second time, because the first time was under Moses. Highlight it: the remnant of his people, left “from Assyria”, modern Turkey, where the Afro-Turks are; “and from Egypt”, lower Egypt, the Afro-Egyptians; “and from Pathros”, southern Sudan; “and from Cush”, Ethiopia; “and from Elam”, Iran and India, the Afro-Iranians, the Siddis and the Dalits; “and from Shinar”, Iraq, the Afro-Iraqis; “and from Hamath”, Syria, the Afro-Syrians; “and from the islands of the sea”, like Cape Verde, the Hawaiian islands and the Melanesian islands.

“And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” That is the all nations of Revelation 7:9: Israel gathered out of them.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Read verse 4 and then verse 9: first the 144,000 sealed of the tribes of Israel, and after this the great multitude. Both are Israel.

Ezra explains it crystal clear. “Arise up and stand, behold the number of those that be sealed in the feast of the Lord”: that is Revelation 7:4, the number that were sealed, the 144. “Which are departed from the shadow of the world, and have received glorious garments of the Lord”: no bodies.

“Take thy number, O Sion, and shut up those of thine that are clothed in white, which have fulfilled the law of the Lord.” They are clothed in white because they have fulfilled the law. “The number of thy children, whom thou longedst for, is fulfilled”: the 144,000. So verses 38 to 41 are Revelation 7:4.

Then verse 42: “I Esdras saw upon the mount Sion a great people, whom I could not number, and they all praised the Lord with songs.” That is Revelation 7:9. The great multitude is Zion, upon mount Sion.

The Bible doesn’t contradict itself. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”: few, because they were killing us. In Hosea 1:10 we are as the sand of the sea that no man can measure nor number, so time has gone by since Moses said we would be few.

“And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone”: Christianity and Islam. “But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him”: from the lands we were taken to, if we seek him with all our heart and soul.

“When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days”. Moses prophesied it: tribulation, in the latter days. The church has taught for years that we don’t have to go through tribulation. You can’t pay your rent, your car got taken, your wife left you: that is not tribulation, that is just bad times. Moses didn’t contradict Christ; the churches contradict the Bible. Moses saw us going through tribulation, the great tribulation the multitude comes out of.

sense.text:
“Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” Moses saw us going through it; the Lord showed Moses the secrets of the times, and showed Solomon and Ezra the beginning, the end and the midst.

A brother asked what makes this tribulation different from all the others, since we caught hell under Babylon, Assyria and the Greeks. Christ already told us in Matthew 24. This tribulation leads into war on the earth, and Christ returns in the midst of it, not only to deliver Israel but for war: tribulation, World War III, then Armageddon. That is why “none is like it.”

precepts.why: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: tribulation, then war on the earth. “And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven”: in verse 30 Christ comes back. In verse 31 the angels “shall gather together his elect from the four winds”, and we say, I’m happy, I’m saved. But that is not all that is going on when Christ returns.

When Christ returns, yes, he is going to deliver us, but something else is going on too. “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: that mushroom effect. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.”

Christ is coming back for war. He is not coming back just to save the Israelites; when he comes back, he is coming back to kill. That is what makes this tribulation different from all the others.

“For, behold, the Lord will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire.” This is what makes it different: in this one, Christ returns.

“For by fire and by his sword will the Lord plead with all flesh: and the slain of the Lord shall be many.” The slain of the Lord ain’t just Esau. You think he is going to let the wicked Israelites do whatever they want to do? They are getting put to death too. All nations are going to get it.

“And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time”. That is saying the same thing as the top of Jeremiah 30:7: “that day is great, so that none is like it”. What makes this tribulation different is World War III and Armageddon.

“And at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.” All nations are not being delivered; Daniel’s people, the Israelites, are: he “shall be saved out of it.” “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

That is the cry of Isaiah 19: spare thy people, because there is going to be death. “Wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?” If their God isn’t helping them.

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” “But I will remove far off from you the northern army”: that is the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16 that is after us. He “will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea”, the Dead Sea, “and his hinder part toward the utmost sea”, the Mediterranean: the land of Israel, what they call the Middle East. “And his stink shall come up”. It is all laid out for us: yes, you’re dying, but you’re not dead; the Lord will cause something to happen over there in the land of Israel and take the northern army down. Tribulation, World War III, Armageddon.

What happens when he removes the northern army? “Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman”. Teman is still Edom. “Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out”: the least of the flock is these Israelis, the fake Israelis, in that whole area on the map. “Surely he shall make their habitations desolate with them.”

“The earth is moved at the noise of their fall, at the cry the noise thereof was heard in the Red sea”: ships in the Red Sea are going to hear about this fall. “Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah”: America is going to come to Israel’s rescue, so they think. Bozrah is Jordan. “And at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of Edom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.” They are going to be afraid, because they don’t realize it is a trap. NATO turns against them; everybody is against America and Israel. That is what is going to happen.

“He shall send them a saviour, and a great one, and he shall deliver them” is saying the same thing as Jeremiah: “Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it: it is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.” They cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors in Jacob’s trouble, and he sends them Christ and delivers them.

sense.text: “For it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him”. That is Christ’s return.

“But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.” David is alive in these last days. But we don’t know who’s who. In the old school they used to say, this one’s David, and it caused a lot of partiality and problems. Don’t do that. Don’t guess who you are; calling yourself Samson, you ain’t nothing.

“Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the Lord; neither be dismayed, O Israel”. He tells us not to be afraid, but the things he tells us are going to happen will make us afraid. Who wants to go through tribulation? That is why we have to increase our faith and remind ourselves this is not the real us; this is just a shell, and the real us is within. “For, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return”, return to the land, “and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.”

“For I am with thee, saith the Lord, to save thee: though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee: but I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.”

“For thus saith the Lord, Thy bruise is incurable, and thy wound is grievous.” “There is none to plead thy cause”: there is none to stand up on our behalf. “Thou hast no healing medicines.” Every negro that just popped out of his mama has a new idea how to save black people, and it is always economics or voting. Those medicines don’t work. The bruise and the wound are our sins, and the only one that can save us is the saviour Jesus Christ, our master, our king, our rabbi.

“All thy lovers have forgotten thee; they seek thee not”. Our lovers are our allies: my Chinese friends like us, my Arab friends like us. In the Bible we always made an allegiance with Egypt or Ethiopia, Ammon or Moab. “For I have wounded thee with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the multitude of thine iniquity; because thy sins were increased.” Our sins are increased: the Houston rodeo with black men and black women whoring themselves out, filthy as hell, so they had to put a dress code on black women; in Nigeria’s Delta State, an alleged festival where women are raped openly in the streets. That is evil.

“Why criest thou for thine affliction? thy sorrow is incurable for the multitude of thine iniquity: because thy sins were increased, I have done these things unto thee.” The Lord did these things, because of our sins.

“Therefore all they that devour thee shall be devoured; and all thine adversaries, every one of them, shall go into captivity”. Every one of our enemies, not some of them. “And they that spoil thee shall be a spoil, and all that prey upon thee will I give for a prey”: P-R-E-Y. All the nations that preyed upon us shall be a prey unto us.

“For I will restore health unto thee, and I will heal thee of thy wounds, saith the Lord”. The only one that can restore our health, going back to verses 12 and 13, is the Lord. There is no magic voting right and no economic situation to save us. How does he heal us? When he sent Christ to die on the cross: by his stripes we are healed. That is the prophecy.

“Because they called thee an Outcast”: African-American, the made-up names they gave our race. “Saying, This is Zion, whom no man seeketh after”: nobody gives a damn about blacks and Latinos.

“Behold, I will bring again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have mercy on his dwellingplaces”. Jacob’s tents are the camps of the tribes, restored again. “And the city shall be builded upon her own heap”: that land is going to be destroyed, and it is going to be built again. “And the palace shall remain after the manner thereof”: the palace is the temple that is going to be built.

“And out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of them that make merry”: we are going to be happy and joyous. “And I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they shall not be small.” There is more in that verse than it seems: we are not going to have these little bodies we have now, frail and skinny, or fat either.

“Their children also shall be as aforetime, and their congregation shall be established before me”. The Lord returns it all back to the way it was, our glorious state. “And I will punish all that oppress them”: all, not some. All that have oppressed us shall be punished.

“And their nobles shall be of themselves”: our nobles are going to come from our own people. We are not going to have nobles of another race, like the mayor they have in New York now. “And their governor shall proceed from the midst of them”: Christ is our governor, and he came from the midst of us. “And I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto me”.
“And ye shall be my people, and I will be your God.”

“Behold, the whirlwind of the Lord goeth forth with fury, a continuing whirlwind: it shall fall with pain upon the head of the wicked.” “The fierce anger of the Lord shall not return, until he have done it, and until he have performed the intents of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it.” Twelve tribes.

precepts.why: “For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim”. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king”. We are returning now; we are seeking the Lord our God. It is telling you David is going to be alive in these last days.

“There is no remembrance of former things”: David will not remember who he is. “Neither shall there be any remembrance of things that are to come with those that shall come after.” Our minds are wiped; we don’t know who’s who. That is why it says love your neighbour as yourself: you don’t know who’s who. And it is a good thing, because guessing who is David caused a lot of partiality and problems.

“And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.” The Lord raises up David again over Israel. Don’t be trying to guess who you are; you don’t know, brother.

Why is he going to make a full end of all nations? “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”. All these nations were born in vain. They are extras in the movie, not the stars; we are. Esau is the villain, the antagonist.

It says the same thing. “Ah sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters”. We are a sinful nation, a people laden with sin; iniquity is sin. “They have forsaken the Lord, they have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward.” “Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more”: our people get punished and revolt more and more against God.

“The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint.” The whole head of the Israelites is sick. “From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.” Not mollified with ointment means no medicine. There is no healing for us. The only one that can save us is the saviour Jesus Christ. That is the bruise that is incurable and the healing medicines we do not have in Jeremiah 30.

What we read in Isaiah 1 is what Job went through. We read Job and say, that was only him, but Job’s real life symbolizes the nation of Israel. “So went Satan forth from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.” That was the fifth judgment on Job: from the sole of the foot, the same as Isaiah 1 and Jeremiah 30. What Job went through is what we as a nation are going through.

Job had friends that did not stand up on his behalf; they were always telling him he was wrong, he was evil. There was none to plead his cause and no cure: God had to intervene and heal Job. That is why the Lord sent Christ to heal the twelve tribes of Israel. Job’s life is Deuteronomy 28: he lost his businesses, his family, everything. His wife turned on him in his darkest moment when he lost everything, and that is how these black women do us. But at the end of Job’s life he got blessed, and that is what is going to happen if we endure to the end.

“And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies”. God walked contrary to us because we kept breaking his laws, and brought us into the land of our enemies. “If then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity”. That is what we have to do: as we repent, accept that God is right and we are wrong. We have always been wrong, and God was just when he punished us.

When your child plays in the street or with the light socket, you beat that behind, not because you hate him, but so he knows you don’t play in traffic or with electricity; you will die. Some talking don’t do good for some kids. That is what God did with us. That is why he says, I have done these things unto thee.

precepts.why:
“And they walked in the midst of the fire, praising God, and blessing the Lord.” They are in the midst of the fiery furnace, praying in song to God. They were in the fire because they would not worship Babylon’s god, and what we read about them is a reflection of what is going to happen to us.

“Blessed art thou, O Lord God of our fathers: thy name is worthy to be praised and glorified for evermore”. “For thou art righteous in all the things that thou hast done to us: yea, true are all thy works, thy ways are right, and all thy judgments truth.” Everything God has done to our race, he is justified, because we revolted against him. They say it because of what Moses said in Leviticus: if we accept the things God has done to us, God is right and we are wrong.

“In all the things that thou hast brought upon us, and upon the holy city of our fathers, even Jerusalem, thou hast executed true judgment: for according to truth and judgment didst thou bring all these things upon us because of our sins.” “For we have sinned and committed iniquity, departing from thee.”

Christianity has done the opposite to our people. A young black man in a clip mocks: you worship a God that got mad at his own people and almost annihilated them for worshipping a piece of gold. This is what Christianity has done to our people.

“And the people, when they knew it, followed him: and he received them, and spake unto them of the kingdom of God, and healed them that had need of healing.” Christ is the only one that can heal us of all these things.

He is the saviour; he is the physician. “They that are whole have no need of the physician”: if you think you’re good and know everything, you don’t need the Son of God. “But they that are sick”: you have to admit you are sick, in the midst of sin, and that all we have done has been wrong. “I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” I didn’t call you righteous, brothers and sisters; I came for sinners.

This goes with Christ saying he came not for the righteous but for sinners. “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not”. Like the disciples, we didn’t wake up one day searching for the Lord of heaven and earth; the word was introduced to us and woke us up. “Unto a nation that was not called by my name”: we are called African-Americans, Haitians, Jamaicans, Puerto Ricans.

“I have spread out my hands all the day unto a rebellious people, which walketh in a way that was not good, after their own thoughts”: we are that rebellious people, in Christianity and Islam, following our own thoughts. “That sacrificeth in gardens, and burneth incense upon altars of brick”: the churches and the mosques. “Which eat swine’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels”: the church always had a swine fest at the end, pig feet, possum soup, turtle soup.

“Which say, Stand by thyself, come not near to me; for I am holier than thou.” That is what the churches say to the Israelites preaching on the street: I’m good, I don’t need no black Jesus, I’m washed in the blood of Jesus, I am water baptized, I am holier than thou. “These are a smoke in my nose, a fire that burneth all the day.” God can’t stand them. They are the whole that think they have no need of the physician.

“Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree”: Christ bare our sins, in his own body, on the tree, which is the cross; the cross was made from a tree. “That we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.” We are healed by Christ’s punishment, his crucifixion. That is how the Lord restores our health and heals us of our wounds: when he sent Christ to die on the cross.

“And the children of Israel shall pitch their tents, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, throughout their hosts.” Every man by his own camp: Judah with Judah, Ephraim with Ephraim, Benjamin with Benjamin. It is the restructuring, the restoration of a nation. Every man by his own standard: Judah had the standard of the lion, Benjamin the wolf, Naphtali the deer, Ephraim the bull. All this is being restored again when he brings again the captivity of Jacob’s tents.
“How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, and thy tabernacles, O Israel!” The tents of Jacob are being restored again.

“He cast out the heathen also before them, and divided them an inheritance by line, and made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents.” Jacob’s tents are the tribes of Israel dwelling in their inheritance, and that is what the Lord brings again.

The city shall be builded upon her own heap and the palace shall remain. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee: for in my wrath I smote thee, but in my favour have I had mercy on thee.” “The glory of Lebanon shall come unto thee, the fir tree, the pine tree, and the box together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary”: that is the palace. “And I will make the place of my feet glorious”: Jerusalem glorious again.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.” “A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” That is why we went there: I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; they shall not be small.

“And I will turn my hand upon thee, and purely purge away thy dross, and take away all thy tin”. “And I will restore thy judges as at the first”. That is what Jeremiah 30:20 says: their children as aforetime, their congregation established. The Lord is going to return it all back to the way it was, our glorious state.

“The Lord also shall save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem do not magnify themselves against Judah.” “And he that is feeble among them at that day shall be as David”: the feeble Israelites are going to be like King David. “And the house of David shall be as God”: the house of David is the 144,000. “As the angel of the Lord before them.” Our glorious state restored.

For the bottom of verse 20, “and I will punish all that oppress them”: “He shall judge the poor of the people, he shall save the children of the needy, and shall break in pieces the oppressor.” There is no coming together and joining with the oppressor. He said he is going to break them.

“And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel.” That is Christ: the governor that proceeds from the midst of us.
